sentences.en: A strict observance of the great traditions of the sea towards women and children reflects nothing but honour upon our civilisation.
sentences.zh: 严格遵守对待妇女和儿童的伟大航海传统，这只会为我们的文明增光添彩。

sentences.en: Even I hope it may mollify some of the young, unmarried lady teachers who are so bitter in their sex antagonism and think men so base and vile.
sentences.zh: 甚至我希望这能平息一些年轻未婚女教师的怒火，她们对男性的性别敌意如此强烈，认为男人如此卑劣下作。

sentences.en: I cannot help feeling proud of our race and its traditions as proved by this event.
sentences.zh: 这一事件证明了我们种族及其传统的伟大，我不禁为此感到自豪。

sentences.en: Boatloads of women and children tossing on the sea, safe and sound, and the rest, silence, honour to their memory.
sentences.zh: 满载妇女和儿童的救生艇在海上颠簸，平安无事，而其余的人，唯有沉默，向他们的记忆致敬。

sentences.en: In spite of all the inequalities and artificialities of our modern life, at the bottom, tested to its foundations,
sentences.zh: 尽管我们现代生活中存在种种不平等和人为因素，但在最底层，在经受住考验时，

sentences.en: our civilisation is humane, Christian and absolutely democratic.
sentences.zh: 我们的文明是人道的、基督教的，并且是绝对民主的。

sentences.en: How differently Imperial Rome or Ancient Greece would have settled the problem.
sentences.zh: 帝国罗马或古希腊处理这个问题的方式会大不相同。

sentences.en: The swells and potentates would have gone off with their concubines and pet slaves and soldier guards,
sentences.zh: 那些权贵和统治者会带着他们的妃嫔、宠物奴隶和卫兵逃之夭夭，

sentences.en: and whoever could bribe the crew would have had the preference and the rest could go to hell.
sentences.zh: 而任何能贿赂船员的人都会获得优先权，剩下的人就去见鬼吧。

sentences.en: But such ethics could neither build Titanics with science, nor lose them with honour.
sentences.zh: 但这样的道德准则既造就不了泰坦尼克号这样的科学结晶，也无法在沉没时保持荣誉。

sentences.en: So that, of course, was Winston Churchill.
sentences.zh: 所以，那当然是温斯顿·丘吉尔写的。

sentences.en: And he was writing a letter, Tom, to his wife, Clementine, after he'd been reading about the loss of the Titanic on the 15th of April, 1912.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，那是他在1912年4月15日读到泰坦尼克号沉没的消息后，写给妻子克莱门汀的一封信。

sentences.en: And it's very Churchill, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这非常有丘吉尔的风格，不是吗？

sentences.en: To have a go at unmarried lady teachers at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 开头就先抨击一下未婚女教师。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I hope any feminists out there listening to that will fill themselves, put in their place.
sentences.zh: 是啊，所以我希望听到这段话的女权主义者们能感到满足，知道自己的位置。

sentences.en: But also to congratulate Britain and the Anglo-Saxon race, as he would have called it, on their splendid performance in the Titanic drama.
sentences.zh: 但同时，他也祝贺英国和盎格鲁-撒克逊种族（正如他所称的那样）在泰坦尼克号这场悲剧中的出色表现。

sentences.en: So the fact that Britain's most expensive and largest ship has sunk the bottom of the ocean is a tremendous reflection.
sentences.zh: 所以，英国最昂贵、最大的船沉入海底这一事实，是一个巨大的反思。

sentences.en: Hurrah for us.
sentences.zh: 为我们欢呼吧。

sentences.en: But also to offer some thoughts about history, profound historical lessons.
sentences.zh: 但也提供了一些关于历史的思考，深刻的历史教训。

sentences.en: So Churchill says, Tom, that the men of Imperial Rome or ancient Greece, the swells and potentates, would have gone off with their concubines, their slaves,
sentences.zh: 所以丘吉尔说，汤姆，帝国罗马或古希腊的男人们，那些权贵和统治者，会带着他们的妃嫔、奴隶，

sentences.en: their soldiers, their eunuchs and whatnot, and the rest could go to hell.
sentences.zh: 他们的士兵、太监之类的逃走，剩下的人就去见鬼吧。

sentences.en: That's probably true, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这大概是真的，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's not wrong.
sentences.zh: 他没说错。

sentences.en: Well, I think it's an insane argument to have.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是一个疯狂的争论。

sentences.en: If the Romans had built it.
sentences.zh: 如果那是罗马人造的船的话。

sentences.en: I think rather than try and answer that question, which I think is essentially unanswerable, or very, very complex.
sentences.zh: 我觉得与其试图回答那个问题——我认为那本质上是无法回答的，或者非常、非常复杂——

sentences.en: You know he's right.
sentences.zh: 你知道他是对的。

sentences.en: You know he's right.
sentences.zh: 你知道他是对的。

sentences.en: It's a fascinating example of the way in which the moment the ship sinks, people start projecting their political opinions, their cultural assumptions,
sentences.zh: 这是一个迷人的例子，说明了船沉没的那一刻，人们就开始投射他们的政治观点、文化假设，

sentences.en: the narrative that they want onto it.
sentences.zh: 以及他们想要强加于其上的叙事。

sentences.en: So in another letter, Churchill says to Clemmie that it's a very good story.
sentences.zh: 所以在另一封信里，丘吉尔对克莱米说这是一个非常好的故事。

sentences.en: You know, and that sense right from the beginning, this is an incredible story.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从一开始就有那种感觉，这是一个不可思议的故事。

sentences.en: That influences the way that the news is received.
sentences.zh: 这影响了新闻被接收的方式。

sentences.en: But before we get onto that, how the story of the Titanic comes to be understood, should we just, as it were, literally pick up from where we left off?
sentences.zh: 但在我们讨论那个问题之前，关于泰坦尼克号的故事是如何被理解的，我们是否应该，就像我们刚才那样，从中断的地方继续？

sentences.en: We've got lots of people bobbing around in lifeboats.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多在救生艇上漂浮的人。

sentences.en: And the ship that comes to their rescue a couple of hours too late is the Carpathia, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而那艘迟到了几个小时才来救援的船是卡帕西亚号，对吧？

sentences.en: A Cunarder of all things.
sentences.zh: 竟然是卡纳德航运公司的船。

sentences.en: So Cunard, they're great rifles.
sentences.zh: 所以卡纳德公司，他们是很棒的航运公司。

sentences.en: And Dominic, it's Captain.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，那是船长。

sentences.en: So you have gone on record as being a big fan of Captain Smith.
sentences.zh: 你可是公开表示过自己是史密斯船长的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: Huge fan.
sentences.zh: 超级粉丝。

sentences.en: And in fact, as we sit here recording this, you have as your name on the screen, Captain Smith.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我们坐在这里录音时，你屏幕上的名字就是史密斯船长。

sentences.en: Tommy, you're giving too many insights to the listeners into our working methods.
sentences.zh: 汤米，你向听众透露太多我们工作方式的内幕了。

sentences.en: But we now come to another Captain, and I will leave the listeners to decide which of us this Captain sounds like.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在要谈到另一位船长，我让听众自己决定这位船长听起来像我们中的哪一位。

sentences.en: So this is a man called Arthur Rostron, who is the captain of the Carpathia, small Cunarder, carrying 743 passengers, three days out of New York,
sentences.zh: 这是一个叫亚瑟·罗斯特龙的人，他是卡帕西亚号的船长，一艘小型卡纳德邮轮，载着743名乘客，离开纽约三天，

sentences.en: heading for Gibraltar and Mediterranean ports beyond that.
sentences.zh: 正前往直布罗陀和地中海沿岸港口。

sentences.en: And one of the officers on the ship says of Rostron, I have the greatest respect for him as a seaman, a disciplinarian, and as a man who could take a decision quickly.
sentences.zh: 船上的一名军官这样评价罗斯特龙：作为一名海员、一名纪律严明者，以及一个能迅速做出决定的人，我对他怀有最大的敬意。

sentences.en: He was not the burly type of jolly old sea dog, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，他可不是那种粗壮、快乐的老海狗。

sentences.en: Far from it.
sentences.zh: 远非如此。

sentences.en: He was of thin and wiry build, with sharp features, piercing blue eyes, and rapid, agile movements.
sentences.zh: 他身材瘦削精干，五官锐利，有着锐利的蓝眼睛，动作敏捷迅速。

sentences.en: Well, Tom, I hear you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，汤姆，我听到了。

sentences.en: The sad thing, though, is that everybody remembers Captain Smith, but nobody's ever heard of the other man.
sentences.zh: 但可悲的是，每个人都记得史密斯船长，却没人听说过另一个人。

sentences.en: Well, this is what the rest of history is about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是历史其余部分的内容。

sentences.en: And of course, Captain Smith is the only one of those two characters who's played by the same person who played Theoden, King of Rohan.
sentences.zh: 当然，史密斯船长是这两个角色中唯一一个由扮演洛汗国王希优顿的演员所饰演的人。

sentences.en: And so listeners can indeed draw their own conclusions from the Theoden and Denethor-like dynamic that's going on there.
sentences.zh: 所以听众确实可以从那里发生的希优顿和德内梭尔式的动态中得出自己的结论。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Rostron is the captain of the Carpathia.
sentences.zh: 所以罗斯特龙是卡帕西亚号的船长。

sentences.en: We said last time, didn't we, that his wireless operator was just going to bed.
sentences.zh: 我们上次说过，他的无线电操作员当时正准备睡觉，对吧？

sentences.en: He was literally taking his boots off.
sentences.zh: 他当时真的正在脱靴子。

sentences.en: He's got his headphones on because he's listening for acknowledgement of a message that he sent.
sentences.zh: 他戴着耳机，因为他在等待确认他发出的信息。

sentences.en: And he hears, actually, what he hears.
sentences.zh: 然后他听到了，实际上，他听到的是。

sentences.en: I misspoke in the last episode.
sentences.zh: 我在上一集说错了。

sentences.en: I said he heard their transmissions.
sentences.zh: 我说他听到了他们的传输。

sentences.en: He hears transmissions that are from Cape Cod going to Titanic, basically saying, you know, how are you getting on?
sentences.zh: 他听到的是从科德角发给泰坦尼克号的传输，基本上是在说，你知道，你们进展如何？

sentences.en: Have you sunk yet?
sentences.zh: 你们沉了吗？

sentences.en: So he then sends a message to Titanic saying, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 所以他随后给泰坦尼克号发了一条信息，问发生了什么事？

sentences.en: I'm on my way.
sentences.zh: 我正在赶来。

sentences.en: And they say, come at once, we've struck an iceberg.
sentences.zh: 他们说，快来，我们撞上冰山了。

sentences.en: You're absolutely right to praise Captain Rostron because he basically says, right, get everything ready.
sentences.zh: 你赞扬罗斯特龙船长绝对是正确的，因为他基本上说，好，做好一切准备。

sentences.en: They get there in three and a half hours.
sentences.zh: 他们在三个半小时内就赶到了。

sentences.en: They're firing rockets to say help is coming.
sentences.zh: 他们发射火箭以示救援正在赶来。

sentences.en: And they've got all their lifeboats ready and all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们准备好了所有的救生艇，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: They've got all their crew ready to haul these guys up.
sentences.zh: 他们让所有的船员准备好把这些人拉上来。

sentences.en: And actually, they perform splendidly, don't they?
sentences.zh: 实际上，他们表现得非常出色，不是吗？

sentences.en: Tremendously.
sentences.zh: 非常出色。

sentences.en: And they actually see the iceberg, which I hadn't realised.
sentences.zh: 而且他们实际上看到了那座冰山，我之前没意识到。

sentences.en: Yeah, a double-toothed iceberg, they describe it as, don't they?
sentences.zh: 是的，他们形容那是双齿冰山，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, double-toothed, looking very menacing.
sentences.zh: 是的，双齿，看起来非常凶险。

sentences.en: A hundred feet high, yeah.
sentences.zh: 一百英尺高，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: As they bring the survivors on board,
sentences.zh: 当他们把幸存者带上船时，

sentences.en: Rostron says, the thing that strikes them is they are silent.
sentences.zh: 罗斯特龙说，让他们印象深刻的是他们非常安静。

sentences.en: There's no noise, no hurry.
sentences.zh: 没有噪音，没有匆忙。

sentences.en: They came solemnly, dumbly, out of a shivering shadow.
sentences.zh: 他们庄严而沉默地从颤抖的阴影中走出来。

sentences.en: I mean, they are broken.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们崩溃了。

sentences.en: They're traumatised.
sentences.zh: 他们受到了创伤。

sentences.en: They're frozen.
sentences.zh: 他们冻僵了。

sentences.en: I mean, they're incredibly cold.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们冷得难以置信。

sentences.en: And among the traumatised is Ismay.
sentences.zh: 在这些受创伤的人中就有伊斯梅。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Who is not saying a word.
sentences.zh: 他一言不发。

sentences.en: He's given a sedative, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他被注射了镇静剂，对吧？

sentences.en: And he basically stays hidden in the ship's doctor's cabin.
sentences.zh: 他基本上一直躲在船医的舱室里。

sentences.en: The billionaire's widows, so Aster, Thayer, Widener, they're given cabins.
sentences.zh: 那些亿万富翁的遗孀们，比如阿斯特、塞耶、怀德纳，她们被安置在客舱里。

sentences.en: By and large, they're put in the dining rooMs.
sentences.zh: 大体上，她们被安置在餐厅里。

sentences.en: And doctors are kind of going round, sort of sorting them out, giving them, I don't know, brandy or whatever they would do.
sentences.zh: 医生们在四处走动，照顾她们，给她们，我不知道，白兰地或者他们会做的任何事情。

sentences.en: And the terrible stories of mothers with very small babies having to use napkins as nappies or diapers as Americans, we call it.
sentences.zh: 还有那些带着很小婴儿的母亲不得不把餐巾当尿布用的可怕故事，或者像美国人说的那样叫纸尿裤。

sentences.en: Oh, God, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，是的。

sentences.en: Anyway, but at least they're alive, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 总之，但至少她们还活着，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What about the dead?
sentences.zh: 那死者呢？

sentences.en: So maybe a little bit of a survey of the dead.
sentences.zh: 所以也许可以对死者做一个小小的调查。

sentences.en: We don't know exactly how many people died because we don't know exactly how many people were on the ship.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道确切有多少人死亡，因为我们不知道船上到底有多少人。

sentences.en: So the official US estimate is 1,517 people.
sentences.zh: 所以美国官方估计是1517人。

sentences.en: The official British estimate is 1,503 people.
sentences.zh: 英国官方估计是1503人。

sentences.en: Somewhere in between those two figures seems reasonable.
sentences.zh: 这两个数字之间似乎是合理的。

sentences.en: And 700 of those are members of the crew.
sentences.zh: 其中700人是船员。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: The biggest loss of life in maritime history other than in battle.
sentences.zh: 这是海事史上除战争外伤亡人数最多的一次。

sentences.en: To that point.
sentences.zh: 在那之前。

sentences.en: And in Britain, it's a greater loss of life than the British had lost in any of the battles of the Boer War, which was the last big war they had fought.
sentences.zh: 在英国，这比英国在布尔战争（他们打过的最后一场大战）中任何一场战役的伤亡人数都要多。

sentences.en: And actually, Richard Davenport Hines in his book, Titanic Lives, has really dug into the stats about why you live and why you die.
sentences.zh: 事实上，理查德·达文波特-海因斯在他的书《泰坦尼克号人生》中深入研究了关于为什么你会活下来而为什么你会死去的统计数据。

sentences.en: And it is pretty clear that you live if you're a woman and you die if you're a man.
sentences.zh: 很明显，如果你是女性，你就能活下来，如果你是男性，你就会死。

sentences.en: That's much more important than class.
sentences.zh: 这比阶级重要得多。

sentences.en: But there is a slight class.
sentences.zh: 但确实存在轻微的阶级差异。

sentences.en: Oh, there is an absolutely a class dimension.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对存在阶级维度。

sentences.en: But if you're a third class woman, you are far more likely to survive than a first class man.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一名三等舱女性，你存活的可能性远高于一名一等舱男性。

sentences.en: But having said that, out of 324 first class passengers, 201 survive.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，在324名一等舱乘客中，有201人幸存。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Out of 277 second class passengers, 118 survive.
sentences.zh: 在277名二等舱乘客中，有118人幸存。

sentences.en: Out of 708 third class, 181 survive.
sentences.zh: 在708名三等舱乘客中，有181人幸存。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of this, the general sense is that a lot of this is determined by access to the boat deck.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很大程度上是因为人们普遍认为这很大程度上取决于能否到达甲板。

sentences.en: So first class passengers are closer.
sentences.zh: 所以一等舱乘客离得更近。

sentences.en: They have more stewards assigned to them per person, stewards who are getting them to the decks.
sentences.zh: 他们每人分配到的乘务员更多，乘务员会带他们去甲板。

sentences.en: Of course, we described in the last episode how the gates are left closed, blocking third class passengers from getting up.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们在上一集描述过闸门是如何保持关闭的，阻挡了三等舱乘客上去。

sentences.en: But not deliberately, just to reiterate that.
sentences.zh: 但不是故意的，只是重申一下。

sentences.en: Not deliberately, but for about half an hour or so, I think.
sentences.zh: 不是故意的，但我想大概持续了半小时左右。

sentences.en: So they're open about 1230, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 所以他们大约在12点30分打开，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So actually longer than half an hour, in other words.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上比半小时要长，换句话说。

sentences.en: It's about 45 minutes.
sentences.zh: 大约45分钟。

sentences.en: If you're in a large family, you're more likely to die because large families...
sentences.zh: 如果你在一个大家庭里，你更有可能死亡，因为大家庭……

sentences.en: Are not going to break up.
sentences.zh: 是不愿意分开的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And just to give the gender figures, Dominic, 74.3% of female passengers survive.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，给出性别数据，74.3%的女性乘客幸存。

sentences.en: 52.3% of children survive.
sentences.zh: 52.3%的儿童幸存。

sentences.en: 20% of men survive.
sentences.zh: 20%的男性幸存。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that gives you a sense.
sentences.zh: 所以这让你有个概念。

sentences.en: And of course, basically what you want to be is a first class woman because 97% of them live.
sentences.zh: 当然，基本上你想要成为一等舱女性，因为她们中有97%的人活了下来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In third class, it's dropped to 47%.
sentences.zh: 在三等舱，这个比例下降到了47%。

sentences.en: But that, as we said, is probably because of distance.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们所说，这可能是因为距离的原因。

sentences.en: One other thing that's really interesting is why the figure's not better for second class
sentences.zh: 还有一件事非常有趣，为什么二等舱乘客的数字没有更好，

sentences.en: passengers because they actually have easier access to the deck than third class passengers.
sentences.zh: 因为他们实际上比三等舱乘客更容易到达甲板。
